slides.headline:
When staff leave,
does their *access*
leave too?
slides.sub: A survey published this week says, for most firms, it doesn't.

slides.statement: of people who left a job could *still* get into sensitive company information afterwards.
slides.source: Sagiss survey of 1,000 US adults via Pollfish, Sept 2026 (published 4 Nov 2026)

slides.title:
Smaller firms are
*more* likely to
leave doors open
slides.source: Share who kept at least one working account after leaving. Sagiss, Sept 2026

slides.statement: said nobody clearly owned the job of *switching off* their access.
slides.source: Sagiss survey of 1,000 US adults via Pollfish, Sept 2026

slides.title:
A simple leaver
checklist
items: Keep one list of every system
Email, CRM, accounting, cloud storage, social accounts, Wi-Fi.
Switching off access is a named task, not everyone's.
Do it on their last day
Any login more than one person knew.
Try the old logins and make sure they're dead.

slides.headline:
Access should be
*one switch*, not a
scavenger hunt.
slides.body: In every CRM we build, each person sees only what they need, and a leaver's access comes off in one place.
